text: this shit a mothafuckin lay-up, i been steph curry with the shot
annotation: Stephen Curry is a professional basketball player for the Golden State Warriors. He’s known for his exceptional shooting ability – in fact, President Barack Obama and many others have crowned him the best shooter they’ve ever seen. Drake considers himself to be a sharpshooter because he hasn’t missed on tracks.

text: brash as fuck, breachin all these aqueducts
annotation:
Earl acts tough, but he’s actually ready to explode emotionally. A breached aqueduct would be exploding outward because of the water pressure. This may also be alluding to tears.



In his March 2010 song “Kill,” he also referenced aqueducts:

At the airport smokin' hash with all the fuckin' baggage handlers
Flowin' like the mothafuckin' aqueducts

Could also be a reference to kids sneaking into the aqueducts of Cali to skateboard as the OF crew are known to do.

text: super rich kids with nothin but loose ends
annotation:
The phrase “loose ends” has some different meanings: these kids have all kinds of loose cash to spend, but that cash can’t solve a lot of their problems,



The term “loose ends” represents unachieved goals due to a lack of ambition. Rich kids often have many opportunities, but no incentives to prosper in terms of self-fulfillment. These children would rather live hedonistic lives, as described on the track.

text: double d, big full breasts on my baby
annotation:
“Double D” or “DD” refers to the bra size of his partner. Women with “double D’s” are considered well endowed; Frank’s partner here has “big, full breasts.”

Frank introducing this woman with her bra size sets the tone for the song. Seeing as the song is more or less about a woman who once had ambitions to thrive in a traditional life getting “lost” in a materialistic, thrilling lifestyle, it’s fitting that Frank describes her firstly by sexually objectifying her. Seeing as big breasts tend to be the beauty standard in America, Frank suggests that this girl is getting acquainted with this lifestyle quite well.

text: bad luck to talk on these rides, mind on the road, your dilated eyes watch the clouds float
annotation:
The mention of “dilated eyes” introduces a double entendre, with “ride” either referring to driving the Ferrari or a high which both Frank and his lover are experiencing.

Talking can interrupt the concentration required to drive a sports car, and it’s not always the smartest thing to do while you’re high.

The white Ferrari, therefore, may refer to the car or to an expensive cut of cocaine.

text: elephant tusk on the bow of a sailing lady, docked on the ivory coast
annotation:
These lines begin the usage of the white imagery portrayed throughout the song. Ivory is a color that’s an off-white. The image depicted is one in which a boat is docked in Cote d'Ivoire, a country known as the Ivory Coast.

The Ivory Coast has a long history with elephants and ivory  poaching. This country used to be filled with elephants, but currently, the population is under the threat of extinction due to poaching.

Elephants are poached for their ivory tusks, which are very valuable. The tusks being on the bow of a sailing lady (a ship) shows that they’ve already been killed. If you’d like to help stop elephant poaching, check out the Bloody Ivory website.



“Elephant tusks of the bore of a sailing lady docked on the Ivory Coast” might also refer to the slave trade and the money Europeans made off black bodies. The old money that helps them afford their Mercedes in a row, winding down the road…

These lines also bring to mind the Greek goddess Atalanta. Listen to how Frank pronounces “bow” like a bow and arrows, not like the bow of a ship. She has been depicted as carrying her arrows in an ivory quiver, and was, herself, a sailor. Her mythology involved sailing and the ocean. Numerous ships have been named Atalanta over the years, and of course, the city of Atlanta itself.



Another interpretation of these lines portray a reference to the ivory figureheads on slave ships (above), ornately decorated with the trappings of wealth, concealing squalor below deck. The comparison between “clean” white and “dirty” black takes on a new level of irony here, as it really the white slavers who are “dirty” in the figurative sense.

To tie it all back in to elephant poaching, note that these ships held cargo not only of human chattel, but also of ivory. When the wreck of the Dutch slaver Fredenborg was salvaged by divers, they found elephant ivory in the wreck. One can only imagine that the more readily dissolvable bones of slaves might also have been found.

text: well, frankly, when that ocean so mufuckin good, make her swab the mufuckin wood, make her walk the mufuckin plank
annotation: Andre starts it off with a clever reference to his collaborator’s name, then continues the ocean metaphor. Swabbing the deck and walking the plank are both activities that might take place on a ship, and given that they involve wood, they fit neatly into sexual double entendres.

text: i could never be nobody number-one fan, your first number one, i had to put it in your hand
annotation:
Drake responds to Future, who seemed to go after Drake on “We Don’t Trust You,” the title track of Future’s 2024 collab album with Metro Boomin where he rapped:

You a nigga number-one fan, dog
Sneak dissin', I don’t understand, dog
Pillowtalkin', actin' like a fed, dog
I don’t need another fake friend, dog
Can’t be ‘bout a ho, 'cause we sharin’, dog
In your feelings, nigga, why you playin', dog?

Drake claps back by insisting that he was the one who granted Future his first song to chart number one, which is true: Drake’s “Way 2 Sexy” from his 2021 project Certified Lover Boy was the first song featuring Future to top the Billboard 100.

This also invokes Drake’s reputation as one of the most commercially influential feature artists in popular music history, as he’s helped elevate 33 artists to their highest charting position in the 2010’s and given six artists their first song to chart #1. In the same vein, Drake later insists that he was the sole reason Rick Ross charted in the prime of his career:

Can’t believe he jumpin' in, this nigga turnin' fifty
Every song that made it on the chart, he got from Drizzy

text: all this jewelry aint no use when its this dark
annotation:
Jewelry, especially diamonds, reflect light. This makes them easy to see in the daylight, but if there’s no light to reflect—they’re no use. The exclusivity of the flashy jewels available to the wealthy is canceled out by darkness—their wealth and stature means nothing when they can’t be seen.



Jewelry also flatters one’s appearance and is meant to be attention-grabbing. Since Frank and this person are already hooking up, the goal for a one-night stand, jewelry no longer matters.

It is also common to have the lights off during sex. Describing the scene as “dark” suggests they are engaging, and relishing, in the sexual acts that are mentioned in the chorus.

text: been living in an idea, an idea from another mans mind
annotation:
Frank is living in a society or idea created by another man. This fuels his internal conflict causing him to question where he should be and what he should be doing. Frank is possibly alluding the pressure celebrities face of following the “status quo.”

This could also be a subliminal reference/criticism of traditional religious doctrines (like the Bible) that were written in the patriarchal era of history and are largely viewed as the “proper” standards of morality today.

In a post from his tumblr page, Frank strongly implies unfavorable sentiments toward religion.

With those sentiments in mind, in these lines, Frank is likely also alluding to the irony that so many people dictate the way they live their lives based on doctrines that supposedly come from God, when from his perspective, every popular religious ideology and philosophy is just an idea from the mind of another human being just like him—and in that case, he should be able to live by his own code of conduct instead of blindly obeying other people’s out-dated views.

text: one solar flare, were consumed, so why not spend this flammable paper on the film thats my life
annotation:
Frank is thinking about his mortality. A solar flare just missed Earth in 2012 which could have destroyed much of civilization and NASA says there’s a 12% chance that one could hit Earth in the next 10 years. We have no control over our fate, all it would take is one unlucky event and we would all be powerless. Frank spends much of the album musing on this principle in his own life.

Old-fashioned cameras which were used for movies used a film made from Nitrocelluose, which is incredibly flammable. All it would take is a small flame and it could wipe out the entire film, and even the surrounding building. Inglorious Basterds, which Frank lists as one of his favorite movies, has a famous scene of arson by film reel. In Frank’s case, the paper is the Earth, which could easily be wiped out. He chooses to spend his time on it making the “film that’s [his] life.”

The “flammable paper” also ties into the hedonistic, uber-lux, live-in-the-present mentality of the verse overall. In the next lines, he smokes up, perhaps using flammable rolling paper to achieve his high.

text: speaking of nirvana, it was there
annotation:
In Buddhism, Nirvana is the state of bliss that comes at the end of a soul’s cycle of reincarnation when it lets go of itself and its desires.

Frank Ocean also mentions the concept of Nirvana in the ninth track on Blonde, “Nights:”

Wanna see nirvana, but don’t wanna die yet

Nirvana is often used colloquially to describe a state of total happiness. As he reflects on this past relationship, Ocean mentions that there was a moment or moments where he felt like he had eternal bliss with this other person.




At 3:28 (from this line to the song’s conclusion), “Seigfried” transitions into a keyboard performance credited in the album’s liner notes as a sample of the unreleased track “Untitled” by Rostam.

text: used to only be niggas, now everybody playin
annotation:
Kanye is talking about how black people used to be the only slaves, now due to material objects anyone can be a slave, black, white or yellow. The idea is that money is being used to keep people doing what others want i.e buying expensive brands and conforming with the popularity, so others can benefit from others labor wages. The ones spending all the money are the slaves, the ones making all the money are the leaders. This is an important line for the identity of the “Slaves” mentioned in the song title. Although a large part of the song is explicitly criticizing institutionalized racism in America, lines like this one and the lines that reference the Maybach car company allow “New Slaves” to engage in a Marxist critique of American capitalism.

This anti-consumerist theme in “New Slaves” might be considered hypocritical by some, since West has made his fortune cleverly manipulating consumer tastes through his lines of expensive clothing. In other words, Kanye really has become a “dick” instead of a “follower” and in doing so has perpetuated this cycle of consumerist slavery.

The “niggas” in this line is sampled from Curtis Mayfield’s “Don’t Worry if There’s a Hell Below, We’re All Going to Go”. It was also sampled in Ye’s 2004 hit, “Jesus Walks”.

Steve Stoute’s “The Tanning of America” touches on a similar idea to Ye – the new generation in America is more “pan-ethnic”, “color blind” and cool.

text: yall throwin contracts at me, you know that niggas cant read
annotation:
“You know that niggas cant read” – Chris Rock – Bring the Pain (1996)

http://www.youtube.com/watch?feature=player_detailpage&v=f3PJF0YE-x4#t=209s

He references the common racist stereotype that black people can’t read. This serves as another reference to slaves, who either couldn’t read, had to hide the fact that they could or were straight up lied to. This new slavery involves complex lawyer language written up by the corporations in contracts, you’re just another black man signing a contract. These corporations know this and love it.



In the SNL performance, Ye says “don’t read” which instead shifts the assertion from blacks being stereotypically illiterate to stereotypically lazy.

text: see the shots that i took , wet like im book
annotation:
Devin Booker is a young shooting guard for the Phoenix Suns, who won the 2018 NBA All-Star 3 point contest, and scored 70 points in a game versus the Celtics on March 24, 2017 – the first player to score 70+ points since Kobe’s 81 point game on January 22, 2006. Booker and Drake have shown each other mutual respect in the past: Drake wore Booker’s jersey to his Phoenix show, and Booker responding on Twitter, calling him his “brother.”

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LDbeAjbkp0Q

“Wet” is a term for a player who makes a lot of shots. Drake’s “shots” are the bars he makes on his diss tracks. Whether it be against Meek Mill, JAY-Z, Pusha T, or anyone else Drake has gone against, he feels like he’s hit his shots enough to deem them “wet.”

text: yeah, this shit way too formal, yall know i dont follow suit
annotation:
In their joint interview with GQ, Kylie described Travis' feelings toward the spotlight:

He was whispering to me the whole time. He just doesn’t like taking the photos.

The interview continued, saying Travis hates anything that “slows him down.”

Although Travis claims to not like the celebrity life, he was spotted out with Kylie Jenner at such mega-events as the 2018 Met Gala.



This is also wordplay between the word “suit”—a type of formal attire—and the phrase “follow suit,” which means ‘to conform to society’s rules.’ An example of this was when he encouraged his fans, informally known as “ragers,” to bypass security and rush the stage during his set at the 2015 Lollapalooza music festival, leading to his subsequent arrest on charges of inciting a riot.

text: sun is down, freezin cold, thats how we already know, winters here
annotation:
Drake’s hometown of Toronto, Ontario, Canada usually starts to reach winter temperatures in the middle of November. Around November 20, 2017, meteorological reports registered negative Celsius temperatures there, long before the official start of winter on December 21.

As winter hits, the sun starts to set earlier, and with less sunlight comes lower temperatures. On November 20, the sun in Toronto set around 4:45 PM/EST, and rose in the morning at 7:20 AM.

text: who put this shit together? im the glue
annotation:
Travis is not only an artist, but also a curator in the sense that he plays a directorial role in his songs and projects. This is shown by the many featured artists that Travis utilises uniquely across his discography, most notably T.I.’s spoken word and narration on Rodeo.

ASTROWORLD is no exception—especially on “SICKO MODE.” Drake is used as an opener and a closer, Swae Lee’s vocals are cut off abruptly and the late Big Hawk is sampled throughout as a tribute to Travis' hometown of Houston.

text: different colored chains, think my jeweler really sellin fruits
annotation:
In 2017, Travis commisioned a jeweler to make him a colorful “Flame Boy” chain. He once compared his chain to rainbow colored Fruit Loops cereal, on his 2016 track, “sweet sweet”:

Shout my town, shout my troops (Shout, shout)
Shout my jeweler, made my chain look like Fruit Loops, yuh (It’s lit)
Come get a taste, come get a scoop (Scoop)

text: with a cup in a cup, actavis, thats a double edge, issa knife
annotation:
Actavis is a global pharmaceutical company whose promethazine/​codeine cough syrup is used in the recreational drug beverage lean. “Cup in a cup,” or double cupping, is a technique where one styrofoam cup is placed in another to help keep the drink cold.

Frank Ocean riffs on how drinking lean is a double-edged sword, meaning that it has positive and negative aspects. It can relax you and give you a nice buzz, but its addicting effect has also taken the life of great rappers like Pimp C.

Ocean updates the double-edged sword idiom with a reference to “issa knife,” a phrase made popular by British rapper 21 Savage. In an interview with DJ Vlad, Savage was asked about the significance of the tattoo on his forehead, which many had presumed to be a cross. 21’s deadpan response, “Issa knife,” birthed a meme.




https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_BVDOfg_Sk&t=1s

text: chopper in the sky like a gun trick, clips on clips like mikey
annotation:
Besides being a term for a helicopter, “chopper” is also a slang term for an assault rifle. Thus, a chopper could be in the sky because a helicopter is flying, or because someone is performing tricks with their gun and tossing it in the air.

Frank uses more gun wordplay with “clips,” referring to either the device used to store bullets in a gun, or a video clip. Mikey Alfred is a designer and filmmaker who has done videos for Golf Media, Frank’s good friend Tyler, The Creator’s app.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TDQ4loOYm0Y

text: back into the game and they know rap will never be the same as befo
annotation:
Perhaps an allusion to his changed state of mind, more fully revealed on the song “25 To Life” from the Recovery album

It’s also a reference to how Em is constantly changing the rap game. He was out of the game for awhile, but now he’s back into it, and it’ll be better than it was before. Possibly a reference to how Relapse bombed critically, but he’s learned his lesson and he’ll be better than that now.

text: nuts they go, macadamian, they go so ballistic, woah
annotation:
Macadamian is a type of nut. Eminem drives the stadium crowd “nuts”

Macadamian nut:



 Also, I don’t think it is a coincidence that the Macadamia nut is a very pale/white colored nut…

text: last name ever, first name greatest
annotation:
Despite never releasing a studio album when this song was recorded, Drake is calling himself the GOAT. Ego much?

Fun fact: Em came out on stage at one of Drake’s concerts to perform his verse on this track. After Em spit his verse, Drake called him the “greatest ever”.

text: everybody else basic, you live life on an everyday basis
annotation:
Alludes to the fact that this girl lives her life as if everyday counts.

“Live not one’s life as though one had a thousand years, but live each day as the last.” – Marcus Aurelius

Essentially a YOLO reference.



Or even more appropriate to the Roman Emperor’s words and Kendrick Lamar is the Latin maxim, “carpe diem” which means “seize the day.” While YOLO can be used to vaguely justify acts, no matter what the consequence; in essence “seizing the day” can be an encouragement to live life the best way you can. Lamar’s original statement, when looked at this way, can be more connected to the next verse poetic justice, which is a just end to your actions good or bad.

text: i drop you a pin like im bowlin
annotation:
In bowling, the aim is to knock over the ‘pins’ placed at the end of an alley with a ball.

“Dropping a pin” can also refer to the pick up function on rideshare apps like Uber, where one drops a pin-like icon at the location on a map where you would like to be picked up or indeed have someone else picked up.



This fits with the overall theme of the song too, with transport/delivery and ride-shares all being mentioned previously.

“Dropping a pin” might also refer to taking the anti-anxiety benzodiazepine, Klonopin. It is sometimes called “pins” or “K-pins.” The drug reference also fits with Frank’s mentions in the previous lines of “roofie” (slang for Rohypnol – also a benzodiazepine) and ecstasy.

text: two tattoos, one read, no apologies, the other said, love is cursed by monogamy
annotation:
A perfect apostle for the Church of Yeezy. The tattoos spell out his new philosophy–there’s no shame in rejecting monogamy, as expectations of monogamy doom sacred love. That may not be what most Christian churches teach, but w/evs, ‘Ye’s not going to hell anyway.



“Love is Cursed by Monogamy” can be read in two different ways:


Monogamy is a curse and you cannot express your love and yourself because of that. It’s a chain that doesn’t allow you to give love to anyone that deserve it. You cannot fuck around.
Monogamy is just how the real world is. You cannot pretend to be in love with thousand of women. The only way to find the real love is to choose your own and unique princess.

text: coke on her black skin made it stripe like a zebra, i call that jungle fever
annotation: Kanye might also be making a reference to the belief that Africa was the origin of mankind, saying that the black came first, with the cocaine (white) on top of the black skin

text: wham-wham-wham, bitch, im the baby
annotation:
Lil Baby uses onomatopoeia here to make the noise of a young infant, or in other words, a “lil' baby.”

He makes fun of the childishness of his name, showing that he is self-aware. Being 23 at the time this song was recorded, he obviously is not an infant. He chose the name “Lil Baby” because he “ran around with older dudes.”

Lil Baby revealed in a 2018 interview that it was Offset who came up with this line while they were in the studio together.

text: only real music is gonna last, all that other bullshit is here today and gone tomorrow
annotation:
In the original track, Jimmy Smith actually says

“Jazz is the only real music that’s gonna last…”

For this song, it is edited out to endorse Drake as someone that is making music that will last.

This was originally sampled by Count Bass D back in 2002.

text: i just might learn to speak mandarin, japanese for the yen that im handlin
annotation:
It looks like Jiggaman is having a “pivot” of his own! With over 882 million speakers, Mandarin Chinese is the most popular language in the world. Learning to speak this language would definitely be a good idea, from a business perspective.



As a polished international businessman, Jay knows the importance of the yen (official currency of Japan) for his many business ventures.

Multimillionaires and billionaires invest their money into economies of other countries in case the primary country their money is invested in fails. Jay has so much money that he is investing some into the Japanese economy.

text: you showed me love, glory from above, regard, my dear, its all downhill from here
annotation:
Frank’s reached a high, but this is the pinnacle of their relationship—the pair can only go downhill. However, “downhill” could mean that their relationship will be easy from here. “Uphill” is going to be difficult/hard, and that the hard part is over and it’s all smooth sailing from here on.

Frank says, “Just the same way you showed me love,” recalling the situations in the verse where his lover showed him how to embrace things that weren’t controllable. Frank extrapolates this to include their relationship’s end.

Frank’s song “Golden Girl,” shares a similar story. Frank sings:

If we build a house in paradise, will we get to heaven still?
If we don’t have to live through hell just to get to heaven
I'mma stay right here, with you
Til the hurricane comes, ‘til the tsunami comes

In both situations, a moment of happiness is accompanied by the sense that the destruction of that happiness is inevitable.

Here, the affection Frank receives from his lover is perceived as “Glory from above,” or from God, but the feeling can’t last for mere mortals. Frank acknowledges this more explicitly in the outro, singing “This is life, life immortality.”

text: one thing i know is that i wanna, win so bad, but im not chicago
annotation: According to Tyler via Twitter, this is a play on words. By way of poetic license, Tyler uses “wind” as a homophone for “win”. Thus, Tyler makes the Chicago (aka “The Windy City”) reference. The Windy City in Chicago was founded during gang violence in the age of prohibition which was similar to if you get the wind you get shot. Tyler is saying he wants death or suicide but he isn’t Chicago.

text: living so the last night feels like a past life
annotation:
Frank lives life to the fullest, so he packs an entire lifetime of adventure and action into a single night. The morning after makes the night before seem surreal.

Drug and alcohol use can also make memories feel like a big blur, as if it happened ages ago or in a past life. After a night of wild partying Frank may be feeling these effects the next morning.

Frank may also be swearing off the excess seen previously in the video. He’s attempting to remove himself from a life fueled by drugs and fast women by chasing a sober existence.

text: these bitches want nikes, they looking for a check, tell em it aint likely
annotation:
It’s a triple entendre – looking for a check as in the Nike shoe, cheque as in money and check as in validation from their friends for wearing Nikes.

Frank uses Nike’s famous “swoosh” logo as a metaphor for money. His groupies usually have the same objective: start a relationship with him so they can take advantage of his wealth and get their check.

However, Frank can see through them and tell that they aren’t interested in anything but money. He tells them from the start that if that’s what they’re looking for, then they need to look elsewhere because they’re not going to get it with him.

Nike is also the name of the Greek goddess of victory, which the company is named after.

text: acid on me like the rain
annotation:
This line could refer to Frank Ocean’s drug usage, specifically that of LSD or acid. Frank refers to his usage of acid by comparing it to rain, when he’s at a party: acid is everywhere, almost as if it is raining down from the sky.

This is also a clever line which plays on the idea of acid rain, which is precipitation composed of liquid chemicals as a result of excessive air pollution accumulating in the sky and falling like rain.

Frank may also be making a reference to Chance the Rapper’s “Acid Rain”.

text: you must be on that white like othello
annotation:
Othello is a play by William Shakespeare about a moorish general in Venice who gains prominence in a white society for his military genius. He falls in love with the white Desdemona, the daughter of a Venetian senator.  The image of Othello literally on Desdemona is used by Othello’s enemy Iago to enrage her father:

IAGO:
I am one, sir, that comes to tell you your daughter
And the Moor are now making the beast with two backs.

Othello ends up killing Desdemona over false accusations of infidelity. When he realizes his mistake, the knowledge that she was faithful to him, a “real life angel,” drives him to take his own life.

Othello is also a board game based on black and white pieces being played and flipped.

“On that white” is a reference to cocaine; he’s saying she must be high if she thinks she’s gonna get a ring or money out of him.

Interestingly in the film adaptation of Othello called simply O, starring Mekhi Phifer and Josh Hartnett, the protagonist loses his way after getting involved with the cocaine game.

text: shit went one-eighty on me, please run that back, though
annotation:
Frank Ocean’s life has changed 180 degrees since he released nostalgia, ULTRA in 2011, but as he expresses in his Boys Don’t Cry magazine letter, his teenage years were some of the best of his life. He seems to be grateful for his stardom, but he still catches himself reminiscing over the past.

Assuming this is all freestyle, he could also be kind of segueing into comments to the studio tech. In other words, “This didn’t go where I thought I was going with this, but play it back for me anyway.”

Another (vague) possibility is that this is a continuation of the message to Chris Brown: “This ‘track’ (conflict) wasn’t supposed to turn into a brawl, but here we are.  Come at me bro”…To support that, the intervening stuff about where Frank’s from could be interpreted as “we don’t fuck around where I’m from”.

text: you really pipin up on these niggas, you gotta be nice for what to these niggas
annotation:
Here Drake takes the perspective of a woman in our current society and comments on the hypocrisy they face.  Especially in the rap/hip-hop industry, women are often objectified.  Drake questions this practice, asking why women are held to such a high standard of respecting men but not vice-versa.  Why would a woman go out of her way to respect a man when she does not get respected or treated well in return?

Additionally, this woman is financially stable and has no need to rely on a man to support her, furthering her independence.

text: head was clean, tony fantano
annotation:
Merlyn shouts out popular music reviewer and the self-proclaimed “internet’s busiest music nerd,” Anthony Fantano a.k.a. TheNeedleDrop.

“Head was clean” has two contexts: Anthony Fantano’s bald head, and the girl described in the previous line being good at performing oral sex (which “head” is slang for).

Fantano responded to this namedrop on Twitter, and later raved about it in a YouTube video:

https://youtu.be/XaSOwoyRoEc?t=1m30s

Fantano has been complimentary of the band’s work, with his greatly positive review of SATURATION bringing new attention to the group.

The two later met for an interview where Merlyn jokingly admitted that he was specifically thinking of Fantano when he got oral sex:

https://youtu.be/KCmXs_qp02w?t=2m50s

text: ooh, ooh, this unrequited love, to me, its nothin but a one-man cult
annotation:
Un-returned affection can often build to fanatical devotion, especially if you internalize it as Frank Ocean did. Cults are often formed around a charismatic leader who uses his followers to advance his own agenda without truly devoting himself to them. Their followers are often conditioned to believe that there is no way to live outside of the strictures set by the cult leader. People often say love is blind, but these lines go one step further and imply that unrequited love is like being brainwashed.

Jim Jones with a member of the Peoples Temple

Here, Ocean is the only person forming this cult around the object of his affections, leaving him lonely both from unrequited love and from not having other worshippers who understand his devotion.

Ocean’s unrequited love could be for a deity or a romantic interest. While the imagery & title of the song suggest a theological, spiritual love interest, the idea of a one-man cult could represent Ocean feeling entrapped in fondness for a more physical individual who won’t love him back.

text: fuck going platinum, i look at my wrist and its already platinum
annotation:
Drake is metaphorically comparing his platinum Rolex timepiece to the state of his record (despite the fact Take Care and So Far Gone hit platinum)

In an interview with Jet magazine he says

I bought a platinum Rolex, which is something I’ve always wanted. Everybody raps about Rolex — it’s such a fixture in hip-hop music. But only a certain amount of people can get the platinum one… The gold one is a staple, and I had that when I first started; I just always said to myself, ‘Yo I wanna be able to get that platinum one and not have to worry about the price.’ I finally was able to get it this year.



This could be interpreted as another Kendrick shot. The attention Kendrick got from his “Control” verse helped him finally achieve platinum for good kid, m.A.A.d city in Aug. 2013 – about 10 months after it was released. Drake, on the other hand, is downplaying the significance of achieving platinum by saying that in the time it takes to look at his watch, it – NWTS – will have already gone platinum.

text: i piss greatness, like goldish yellow
annotation:
This marks where Wayne starts going off-topic. Only 6 bars in, and he’s already forgotten what the song is actually about.




It looks like Weezy’s moved on from punchlines about poop to a different bodily function. Gold represents value and high quality; everything about Wayne, down to his piss, is of pure excellence.

Wayne’s the rap game Ricky Bobby.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RrvkB3pK8lg

Urine that resembles a goldish yellow color indicates dehydration. Wayne has been working so hard over the years he doesn’t even have the time to keep himself hydrated.

text: rollin marijuana, thats a cheap vacation
annotation:
When you hit the blunt, you relieve stress and visit cloud 9—no need for an airplane ticket.

While some people get away on vacation, smoking some weed is how Frank manages to escape his problems, especially as he mentions he is stressed out. Scientifically, studies have shown that relief from anxiety and stress is the “most commonly reported reason for using marijuana.”

“Cheap vacation” also works as a play on the slang description of taking drugs as “tripping.” Since weed is one of the least expensive and most easily accessible illegal drugs (even becoming legal in some states), it’s literally a “cheap trip.”

text: i been out here head first, always like the head first
annotation:
Frank is saying he’s always been the type to learn from trial and error or going into situations “head first”. The next line is sexual innuendo for oral sex.

The line also serves a double entendre, as babies come out of their mother “head first”, literally.

text: breathe til i evaporated, my whole body see-through
annotation:
Frank might be referencing a smoke session with the person from the previous lines. He hits the bong so much with this person that he starts to evaporate into clouds. In that way, his body becomes transparent like a haze.

“You don’t even got nobody being honest with you…” but Frank is saying, he’s made himself so vulnerable to this person, more so than all this family. As details of the relationship progress, we learn that soon they are only rolling marijuana as a cheap vacation. What was once a vulnerable honest relationship has turned into a cheap, easy escape. We can all relate to those relationships that have digressed from intimate to escape.

“Whole body see through” –
Can be in relation to his response of “nobody being honest with you”. He is transparent compared to these people, he is evaporated.

Also could be in reference to his enthusiasm for cars and how the next line “Transportation, handmade” supports that. The body to his car could be see through meaning you can see the internal specs such as the engine. A handmade car could include this feature.

text: stripper booty and a rack like wow, brain like berkeley
annotation:
UC Berkeley is one of the top universities in the country. This is one smart lady.

“Brain” is also slang for oral sex—she’s also in that department. This quip is similar T.I.’s line in ‘“Whatever You Like.”

Brain so good (good) I swore you went to college

Also, Berkeley has a very liberal history, which is in line with the Coachella festival mentioned next.

For dental school, she’d have to go to UCSF (Berkeley doesn’t have a dental program).

Also, George Berkeley is a famous philosopher, who believed everything is subjective (viz. only in the mind). Ocean is suggesting that this girl may not be real or just a  figment of his imagination (she does seem quite  idealistic). See the music video of this song for clarification on this point.

text: this for yall that think that i dont write enough, they just mad cause i got the midas touch
annotation:
According to the myth, Midas was the king of Phrygia, a Greek polis in Asia Minor. After he did a favor to one of the Gods, he was promised to have one wish granted, and he asked for a golden touch: everything he touches would turn to gold. While at first he was happy with his new gift, he came to suffer for it. Eventually he turned his own daughter into a golden statue.



This may be a reference to this line from “Charged Up” – “I see you niggas having trouble going gold.” While Meek can barely go gold, Drake produces certified “gold material” (500,000+ units sold) without even trying.

text: i could give two fucks bout where the grammys go, i just gave out grammys on my instagram
annotation:
Drake is already a Grammy winner, and has been nominated for more this year without even releasing an album in 2014. Like most of the hip hop community, Drake doesn’t rely on the Grammys to tell him what the best music is.

Drake conducted his own “Hood Grammys" on Instagram, giving out his own personal awards to:



Bobby Shmurda for Vocal Performance of the Year

OG Maco for best all around turn up

Rae Sremmurd and Rich Gang for best performance by a group or duo

And many more.



Drake echoed a similar sentiment during his 2019 Grammys acceptance speech:

You’ve already won if you have people singing your songs word for word…if there’s people who have regular jobs who are coming out in the rain, in the snow, spending their hard-earned money to buy tickets to come to your shows, you don’t need this right here [a Grammy], I promise you, you already won.

text: im fucking on a milf right now, im a motherfucker
annotation:
“MILF” is a sexual term often used as an allusion towards older women—specifically targeted at women above the age of 30, as this is the average age for first-time mothers.

Given the context of the lyric following the line “I’m a motherfucker,” Ken Carson also references what the acronym stands for, with “MILF” being an acronym for “Mother I’d Like to Fuck,” giving the applied thought of Ken’s interest in older women.

text: bar mitzvah money like my last name mordecai
annotation:
Mordecai is a prophet from The Book of Esther in the Hebrew Bible. Haman the Agagite made a decree that all should prostrate themselves before Haman, but Mordecai refused to do so.



It’s only customary to get large sums of money at one’s Bar Mitzvah. Drake’s jewish, so just ask Drake himself.



Drake’s got that Talmud money.

text: cause that truth hurts and those lies heal, and you cant sleep thinkin that he lies still
annotation:
Drake doesn’t want to lie to this girl, but if he tells her the truth it will kill her. Because of his lies, Drake can’t sleep.

Here, Drake plays on the words “lies still”, serving as a double entendre:

Firstly, and most obvious, Drake admits that he (the person he’s talking about) still is lying, making this girl unable to sleep.

Secondly, she can’t sleep as she’s restless, while he is lying still, because he’s sound asleep.

Furthermore, it’s also a play on the previous line. He wants to die real because if he tells her the truth, it’ll hurt her, whereas if he lies, it won’t make her feel as bad.

text: she said, baby boy, why you looking grimy as shit?, ill make the wristwatch flood, let diamonds fill my sink
annotation: i look dirty but i smell good i swear

text: without 40, oli, thered be no me, magine if i never met the broskies
annotation:
Noah “40” Shebib is Toronto native, OVO family member, and Drake’s main musical partner as a producer and engineer. 40’s production has become synonymous with a changing trend in hip-hop.

Oliver North is the nickname for Oliver El-Khatib, Drake’s manager, half of October Firm, and OVO co-founder.

Without them, he wouldn’t be the artist he is today. But, with his friends, ​Drake made an OVO Institution, or a “firm” as Drake preferred to call it during the More Life era.

text: you tried to play nice, everybody just took advantage, you left your fridge open, somebody just took a sandwich
annotation:
Kanye paints the picture of an abusive situation, more so in spirit, of how being nice to other people only proves to be a personal weakness. Being open to others will ultimately lead to them taking something away from you, and in some cases breaking you down.

Rihanna said something similar on “FourFive Seconds”:

Cause all of my kindness
Is taken for weakness

text: and where im walkin, its studded, and half-retarded, i stumble
annotation:
The metaphorical path Earl is walking on is the road through fame, which is filled with all sorts of challenges and stress, such as Earl not even being able to visit his dying Grandmother. while he is finishing this album. Earl could also be adjusting to his new life after being sent to Samoa, before, he was a very chaotic child, rapping in a very horror-core manner throughout his debut mixtape EARL, and now he has to get used to maturing.



Earl also means to literally stumble from being intoxicated, tying into the following line.

text: this a rollie, not a stopwatch, shit dont ever stop
annotation:
“Rollie” is common slang for a Rolex timepiece, while a stopwatch is a very simple timepiece that measures time when activated. The Oyster Rolex models are equipped with self-winding mechanical movement systems which allows for perpetual time keeping in the same way Drake hasn’t stopped and continues to put music out that make the charts.

On Rolexes, as with other high-end mechanical watches, the second hand “sweeps” or “glides”, as opposed to cheaper quartz watches which tick, stopping and starting at each second. Drake’s work ethic is akin to that of a Rolex which never stops.

The Canadian rapper has embraced Rolexes as a symbol of success, as he owns more than several.



Drake is pictured above wearing a Rolex Day-Date, also known as a Rolex President.

text: money for revenge, man, thats hardly an expense
annotation:
During his beef with Pusha-T, Pusha-T claimed that Drake offered $100,000 for any dirt on him.



In this line, Drake addresses the claim, implying that money spent on vengeance is worth it, while also pointing out that the $100k price is nothing compared to the amount of money he makes, as suggested by the rest of the verse.

This line, along with a few others that had been released after “The Story of Adidon” dropped, indicate Drake did in fact capitalize on his offer to gain hurtful information on Pusha-T and Kanye. According to Rap-A-Lot Records CEO and friend J. Prince, Drake had been working on a career ending diss for both rappers before being asked not to release it. A week after Scorpion was released, Drake appeared on London’s Link Up TV, where he rapped in his freestyle, “I know so much shit i can’t expose, I keep it inside and laugh on my own.” One might say Drake believes he already has his revenge on Push and Kanye by having this alleged information in his back-pocket.

text: its hell on earth, and the citys on fire, inhale, in hell, theres heaven
annotation:
Frank is commenting on the current tumultuous and chaotic state of the world. When he smokes, he reaches “heaven,” a happier place that is free of everyday problems.

“Inhale” is a play on “in hell,” which is ironic considering the weed’s feelings of “heaven.” Frank also juxtaposes getting high to opiate his feeling of “so low.”

Furthermore, this continues the theme of choosing between the traditional definitions of heaven and hell. Typically, smoking marijuana would be associated with Hell, but to Frank it is heaven. Within the traditional concept of “Hell” lies Frank’s “Heaven.” Another example in Frank’s music of duality would be his frequently addressing his own bisexuality.

Frank could also be discussing the inherent duality of life. That things are seldom so cut and dry that anything is purely evil or purely good. Even in the worst situations there is good, even “in hell there’s heaven”.

text: i got a record but im clean as they come
annotation: Ameer uses a double entendre of the word record by saying he has a record (album) and criminal record. Saying he’s as clean as they come means he had a clean slate with his criminal record and it also means he’s a clean rapper as he doesn’t swear on this verse.

text: you only live once, thats the motto, nigga, yolo
annotation:
YOLO is the name of a popular restaurant in Miami. Since Drake mentions Miami in this song, it makes sense he’d draw inspiration from a place he’s been.
Another restaurant, Planet Hollywood in Las Vegas, is also called YOLO. The slogan is “You only live once so…live the good life!”

The phrase You Only Live Once went on to become quite the fixture within pop culture.



Additionally, Mac Dre rapped a similar line on “Life’s a Bitch”:

Life is short you only live once and ain’t no telling when your leaving

text: you cut your hair, but you used to live a blonded life
annotation:
“Blonded” here sounds strikingly similar to “blinded.” Perhaps tying this song to the title of the album, and the title to larger themes of carelessness and innocence that has been lost. Both blonde hair and overly long hairstyles have stereotypes surrounding them (blondes are thoughtless, long haired people are careless and/or hippies). Cutting that hair could symbolize growing out of that phase, or distancing themselves from that time.

This may be a reference to the story of Samson in the bible, who, after his hair was cut, lost his strength and was blinded after the Philistines gouged out his eyes.

This may also refer to Frank’s ex, Willy Cartier. Cartier is a French model with signature long hair.



The two dated for a bit in 2012 but the relationship didn’t last—his song feels like an ode to the two of them & their brief past together



It’s unclear whether Cartier actually cut his hair short.
